¿Cómo se calcula el campo magnético de u: How is the magnetic field of a current-carrying wire calculated?
Con la ley de Biot-Savart. Para un hilo: With the Biot-Savart law. For an infinite wire, B = μ₀I/(2πr). For example, with I = 10 A at 5 cm from the wire, B = 4π·10⁻⁷ · 10 / (2π · 0.05) = 4·10⁻⁵ T, that is, 40 μT.
¿Y el de una espira, un solenoide o un t: And that of a loop, a solenoid or a toroid?
En el centro de una espira de radio R, B: At the centre of a loop of radius R, B = μ₀I/(2R). In a long solenoid, B = μ₀nI, with n turns per metre; in a toroid of N turns, B = μ₀NI/(2πr) inside it. For example, a solenoid of 1000 turns/m with 2 A gives B = 4π·10⁻⁷ · 1000 · 2 ≈ 2.5·10⁻³ T.

Integrándola para las formas habituales: Integrating it for the usual shapes gives the expressions the calculator uses:
<b>Hilo indefinido</b> a distancia <i>d<: Infinite wire at distance d: B = μ0I/(2πd), with the field lines in circles around the wire (right-hand rule).
<b>Segmento</b>: <i>B</i> = μ<sub>0</sub: Segment: B = μ0I/(4πd)·(cos α1 − cos α2), where α1 and α2 are the angles between the current and the lines joining each end to the point. A semi-infinite wire is the case α2 = π.
<b>Espira circular</b> de radio <i>R</i>: Circular loop of radius R, on its axis at distance z: B = μ0I R2/(2(R2 + z2)3/2). Off the axis the integral has no simple form and is computed numerically.
<b>Arco</b> de ángulo θ, en su centro: <: Arc of angle θ, at its centre: B = μ0Iθ/(4πR).
<b>Solenoide</b> de <i>N</i> espiras y l: Solenoid of N turns and length L, on the axis: B = μ0NI/(2L)·(cos β1 − cos β2). If it is very long (ideal), B = μ0NI/L inside and 0 outside.
<b>Toroide</b> de <i>N</i> espiras, dent: Toroid of N turns, inside the core at distance r from the centre (Ampère's law): B = μ0NI/(2πr), and 0 outside.
<b>Espira rectangular</b> de lados <i>a<: Rectangular loop with sides a and b: the sum of its four sides; at the centre, B = 2μ0I√(a2 + b2)/(πab).
<b>Cilindro con corriente</b> (macizo, h: Current-carrying cylinder (solid, hollow or from a coaxial cable), with Ampère's law: B = μ0Ienc/(2πr). With uniform J, inside a solid cylinder of radius R, Ienc = I r2/R2; with J ∝ r, Ienc = I r3/R3. In a coaxial cable, outside everything B = 0.
<b>Lámina de corriente</b> indefinida co: Current sheet of infinite extent with density K (A/m): B = μ0K/2 on each side, parallel to the sheet, perpendicular to K and in opposite directions. Between two sheets with opposite currents, B = μ0K, and outside, 0.
<b>Disco cargado que gira</b> con densid: Rotating charged disc with density σ and angular velocity ω: each ring carries dI = σωr dr; at the centre, B = μ0σωR/2.
El campo de varias fuentes es la suma ve: The field of several sources is the vector sum of the fields of each one (superposition). With B you get the Lorentz force on a charge, F = q v × B, and the force on a conductor, F = ∫ I dl × B.
Lejos de una espira, de un solenoide o d: Far from a loop, a solenoid or a rotating disc, the field is that of a dipole of moment $m = I S$ (pointing where a corkscrew turning with the current advances): $B ≈ {μ_0}/{4π r^3}[3(m·r̂)r̂ − m]$, with $μ_0 m/(2π r^3)$ on the axis and $μ_0 m/(4π r^3)$, in the opposite direction, in the plane of the loop. The «Magnetic dipole» question compares it with Biot-Savart. The vector potential $A = {μ_0}/{4π}∮ {I dl}/{|r − r′|}$ satisfies $B = ∇ × A$ and $∮ A·dl = Φ$; in an ideal solenoid it is $μ_0 n I ρ/2$ inside and $μ_0 n I R^2/(2ρ)$ outside, where B is zero but A is not.
Dos hilos indefinidos paralelos al eje Z: Two infinite wires parallel to the Z axis pass through (−a, 0) and (a, 0) with the same current I in opposite directions. At the origin each wire is at distance a and creates B = μ0I/(2πa); both fields point in +Y, so they add:
La fuerza por unidad de longitud entre e: The force per unit length between them is F/L = μ0I2/(2π·2a) = μ0I2/(4πa), repulsive because the currents are opposite. Open it in «Example exercises», in the My exercises bar, to see the full working.
